lines: The air is different down here — stale, heavy with old stone and something chemical you can't quite identify. The Undercity Warrens.
A hidden network beneath Meridian, officially unacknowledged by the Council. Unofficially, everyone knows it exists.
A sign scratched into the wall near the entrance: DEEP ACCESS RESTRICTED — OUTPOST CLEARANCE REQUIRED. A sealed gate waits to the north.

actions.prompt: Elara studies you for a moment, then gives a slow nod. 'New face. Ask what you need to know.'

options.label: What's in the east wing?
options.description: The Luddite cell and what they're guarding.

options.label: What's in the supply crate?
options.description: The locked crate in the corner of this room.

options.label: How do I get through the sealed gate?
options.description: The Ring Authority checkpoint to the north.

lines: Elara leans against the wall. 'Luddite hardliners. Eight to ten fighters — came through maintenance passages from the Nightside undercity about three months ago.'
'They took the east wing and nobody's moved them since. They're guarding something. I haven't been able to find out what, and I'm not in the business of finding out the hard way.'
Elara glances at the supply crate in the corner. 'That came off a Meridian city convoy — the gang intercepted it. I intercepted it back, eventually, but they kept the key.'
'If you find the key in the east wing and come back here, the crate is yours to open. Consider it payment for clearing out the problem.'
Elara shrugs. 'Ring Authority installation — old checkpoint from when the warrens were used for legitimate civil maintenance. Still keyed to Outpost Balor clearances.'
'If you've talked to Warden Holt up at the outpost, you've got the credentials. The gate reads biometrics somehow. Don't ask me how the old tech still works down here.'

actions.prompt: Elara looks up from her work. 'Back again.'

options.label: The supply crate — remind me what's in it.

actions.prompt: Elara leans back, a rare look of ease on her face. 'You cleared the east wing. Means I can move stock again. Need anything?'

options.label: Browse wares.
options.description: See what Elara has for sale.

lines: Elara glances toward the sealed gate to the north. 'With the Luddites gone, the warrens are quiet for the first time in months.'
'I've got contacts deeper in. Supply chain runs slow down here — limited stock, but no Council markups, no questions about where you got it. Come back when you need something.'
Elara shrugs. 'Still there. More disciplined than your average luddite cell — they've got the east wing locked down tight.'
'The iron key should work on the main door. If you've found it, that's your way in.'

actions.text: Elara glances at the crate. 'Medical supplies. Sol grid modifier. City-grade, not frontier scrap. Find the supply crate key and it's yours.'
Elara glances at the empty crate. 'You already took it. We're square.'
A worn iron key, bent but functional. It looks like it fits a reinforced door — the kind used in restricted sections.

lines: A heavy-duty crate key, still attached to a Meridian supply chain tag. This fits the crate in Elara's den.
The gang had it hidden here — whatever was in that convoy, they didn't want anyone getting to it easily.
The supply crate grinds open with a resonant clang. Inside, wrapped in protective cloth: medical supplies and a sol grid component — undamaged despite everything.
Elara was right. Worth the trip.
The last Luddite goes down. The east wing is quiet.
Somewhere behind you, you hear Elara shift. 'That's the last of them. Good work.' A pause. 'Come find me when you're ready. I've got things to move now that the block is clear.'
The warrens are different now. Without the Array's economic pressure above, some of the undercity's informal economy has relaxed — Elara's network has legitimate competitors on the surface.
But the passages are carrying more Unbounded traffic. People moving both ways, exchanging techniques in ways the Council can't easily track or stop.
The warrens have become a recognized transit corridor — the merger protocols established formal channels between the city above, the Unbounded below, and the Underlumen network deeper still.
Elara's operation has gone semi-legitimate. She still moves things, but now some of those things have official stamps on them.
Ring Authority patrols now check the access point above. The warrens are officially under Council jurisdiction.
Elara's corner is empty. The crate is gone. The undercity's informal network has gone either deeper or quiet — it's hard to tell which.
